project.name: Recipe box
project.summary: A tiny web app to keep and browse recipes.

tasks.goal: Serve a home page that shows the app name
tasks.why: One page that answers proves the server, the route and the tests all work.
checklist: Branch feat/skeleton
Answer GET / with status 200 and an HTML content type
Show Recipe box in an h1 heading
Run npm test until it passes
Commit: feat(web): add home page
doneWhen: After npm start, http://localhost:3000 shows Recipe box in a heading

tasks.why: Hosts ping a health URL to know the app is up.
checklist: Answer GET /health with status 200 and a small JSON body
Add test/health.test.js for it
Commit: feat(api): add health check
tasks.doneWhen: GET /health returns 200 and the tests pass

tasks.why: Deploying on day one removes the scariest step early. Every later task ships to a real URL.

learn.label: Render docs: deploy a Node web service

checklist: Push the repo to GitHub
Create a free Render web service from the repo
Set the start command to npm start
Tell Menitor the public URL when it's live
tasks.doneWhen: The public URL shows Recipe box

tasks.goal: List the recipes as JSON at GET /recipes
tasks.why: A JSON endpoint gives the page, and anything later, one place to read recipes from.
checklist: Branch feat/recipes
Add data/recipes.json with three recipes
Answer GET /recipes with the list as JSON
Add test/recipes.test.js for it
Commit: feat(api): list recipes
tasks.doneWhen: GET /recipes returns the three recipes as JSON, and the tests pass

tasks.goal: Show the recipes on the home page
tasks.why: The list is the whole point of the app. Seeing it on the page closes the loop.
checklist: Read the recipes when building the home page
Show each recipe title in a list
Show No recipes yet when the list is empty
Commit: feat(web): show recipes on the home page
doneWhen: The home page lists every recipe title
An empty list shows No recipes yet
